Definitions introduce new objects; theorems prove properties.\n\n## `\\uses` Dependency Guidelines\n- **Statement `\\uses`**: list only what's needed to *state* the result (typically definitions of the objects involved). Keep minimal — transitive deps are automatic.\n- **Proof `\\uses`**: list only what the proof *actually calls*. Don't list definitions unless the proof unfolds that definition.\n- **Never self-reference**: a proof's `\\uses` must NOT include the label of the theorem it proves.\n\n## Recording Formalization-Only Lemmas\nSome Lean lemmas are genuine proof infrastructure rather than named statements\nfrom the original papers. Do not add them only to silence a sync\n  warning; the dependency edge should explain where the auxiliary result is\n  used.\n- Do not mark an auxiliary node with proof-level `\\leanok` unless its Lean proof\n  is complete and `#print axioms` has no `sorryAx`. Statement-level `\\leanok`\n  is acceptable only when the Lean statement is intentionally recorded but the\n  proof remains tracked as incomplete.\n\n## Blueprint Structure\n- `content.tex` is a router: `\\input{chapter/ch01_intro}` etc.\n- Each chapter is a separate file in `chapter/`\n- Definitions/theorems numbered within chapters: `\\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}[chapter]`\n\n## Lean Blueprint Macros\n- `\\lean{Namespace.DeclName}` — links to Lean declaration\n- `\\leanok` — context-sensitive marker; see \"Statement-level vs proof-level `\\leanok`\" below\n- `\\uses{label1, label2}` — declares dependency edges for the graph\n- `\\notready` — marks as not ready for formalization (orange in graph)\n- `\\mathlibok` — already in Mathlib (dark green in graph; see legend note below)\n\n### Statement-level vs proof-level `\\leanok`\n\n`\\leanok` is context-sensitive for human review and graph interpretation. The same macro is used for two different claims, so reviewers should read it by placement rather than by raw token count.\n\n**Statement-level `\\leanok`.** Place this inside a `theorem`, `lemma`, `proposition`, `corollary`, or `definition` environment, on its own line immediately after `\\lean{...}`. This file holds only\nMIPStarRE's project-local facts — it restates no shared rule, and shared\nrules never move here.\n\n## Style (MATHLIB_style)\n\n### Linter warnings\n\nDo not mask linter warnings instead of fixing them. A cleanup PR should not add\nbroad `set_option linter.<name> false` blocks, and especially not file-wide\nblocks, just to make the build output quieter. Linters exist to expose real\nmaintenance problems; hiding them makes later proof work and review harder.\n\nFix the warning at its source whenever possible:\n\n- wrap long lines rather than disabling `linter.style.longLine`;\n- remove or narrow unused variables, section variables, and unused typeclass\n  assumptions rather than disabling the corresponding unused-* linter;\n- remove unused `simp` arguments rather than disabling `linter.unusedSimpArgs`;\n- rewrite proof terms or state the simplified goal explicitly rather than\n  silencing `linter.flexible`.\n\nIf a linter warning is a genuine false positive or a temporary porting\nexception, use the narrowest possible scope, preferably\n`set_option linter.<name> false in <decl>`, and add a short nearby explanation.\nSuch exceptions should be rare and reviewable. Never use linter suppression as\nthe main mechanism for a linter-warning cleanup PR.\n\n## PR review (MATHLIB_pr-review)\n\n### Source-faithfulness checks\n\nFor this repository, the first review question is whether a paper-facing Lean\nstatement still represents the cited result in `references/ldt-paper/`.  Before\napplying the general mathlib review checklist in the lean-conventions\n`MATHLIB_pr-review` reference, compare every changed\nsource-labelled theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary, or definition with the\ncorresponding paper statement and the active blueprint entry.\n\nReject a paper-facing statement if it has acquired a non-paper bridge, residual,\nrepair, package, producer, proof-obligation, assumptions-bundle, hypotheses-bundle,\nor arbitrary implication hypothesis. A source-labelled\nblueprint entry should point to the source theorem or its faithful construction\ntheorem, not to conditional helpers whose assumptions are proof obligations.\nAuxiliary Lean declarations may be recorded in a separate remark, provided the\nremark states that they are not additional hypotheses in the paper theorem.\n\n## Proof integrity (PROOF_INTEGRITY)\n\n### Companion document\n\n> **Companion document:** [`anti_patterns.md`](./anti_patterns.md) catalogues\n> subtler proof-evasion patterns that pass every blocker check in the\n> lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference yet still\n> fail to prove the claimed mathematics (conclusion-shaped hypotheses,\n> definitional sleight-of-hand, zero-fallback branches, trivial default\n> witnesses, Mathlib-bypass castles, external `*Statement` smuggles).\n> Consult it alongside this file during review.\n\n### Project paper-realignment protocol\n\nThe canonical paper-realignment exception in the lean-conventions\n`PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference is instantiated here as\nfollows (the protocol and the `**Unfaithful:**` marker are described in\n`AGENTS.md`):\n\n> **Paper-realignment exception:** When a PR is explicitly realigning a\n> source-labelled declaration with `references/ldt-paper/`, the `sorry`\n> blocker of the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference may be\n> temporarily relaxed for the affected proof bodies. results/telemetry/sessions/reviewer-pr0001-20260830-03.last.md:22:F1. `def:graph-distribution` now correctly requires a nonempty edge set, but `def:typed-cl-distributions` accepts an arbitrary graph and immediately invokes `μ_G`. The source has the same implicit boundary omission at `references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:65-92`, label `def:graph-distribution`, where the normalization is `1/(2m-k)`. Propagate `E ≠ ∅` to the typed definition and downstream uses.
results/telemetry/sessions/reviewer-pr0001-20260830-03.last.md:24:F2. `lem:ld-sandwich` samples uniformly from `Y` without assuming it finite and nonempty. It also post-processes into arbitrary `R_i`, while `def:bracket` at lines 28-38 requires a finite target. The omission is inherited from `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:465-495`, label `lem:ld-sandwich`; the cited `references/neexp-paper/05_quantum_preliminaries.tex:952-973`, label `fact:low-degree-sandwich`, instead uses a specified probability distribution. Add the boundary hypotheses or use finite evaluation images.
results/telemetry/sessions/reviewer-pr0001-20260830-03.last.md:26:F3. By `def:povm-distance` at lines 192-199 and its explicit interpretation at lines 210-212, `A≈_δB` supplies only an `O(δ)` bound. The operator inequalities preserve that hidden constant; they do not prove the literal `≤δ` conclusions at lines 253 and 270. The source repeats the imprecision at `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:347-380`, labels `fact:add-a-proj2` and `lem:cool-closeness-fact`. Replace both final bounds by `O(δ)`.
results/telemetry/sessions/reviewer-pr0001-20260830-03.last.md:28:F4. The paper fixes `N` as the positive integers at `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:4-7` and takes `m,d,ldc∈N` at `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:33-35`, label `sec:ld-game`. At `(q,m,d,k)=(2,1,0,1)`, the blueprint's `δ_ld` is zero for every `ε`; taking `ε=1` admits arbitrary strategies, while deterministic players returning different point values contradict the three exact measurement conclusions. Require `d,k≥1`; any harmless `k=0` extension should be a separate corollary.
results/telemetry/sessions/reviewer-pr0001-20260830-03.last.md:30:F5. `def:ld-win-predicate` replaces the paper's ambiguous zero-direction clause with universal quantification over every valid `t`. That is a defensible correction, but line 146 then falsely says the modified game “coincides” with the external tensor-code test. The source proof at `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:442-454`, label `lem:ld-soundness`, depends on that identity. Specify a canonical zero-direction test and prove the required monotonicity or soundness transfer.
results/telemetry/sessions/reviewer-pr0001-20260830-03.last.md:32:F6. The paper introduces `q,m,d∈N` at `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:903-905`; its `def:admissible` at lines 958-960 adds field admissibility and `m|q` within that positive domain. The blueprint instead calls `(2,1,0)` admissible. Then `δ_qld=0` even for `ε=1`, so `thm:pauli` would map an arbitrary product strategy exactly to an EPR-containing state, impossible under local isometries. The honest line answers and `def:combine-map` also cease to have degree at most zero. Add `d≥1` and revise the `d=0` discussion without discarding the corrected probability calculation.
results/telemetry/sessions/reviewer-pr0001-20260830-03.last.md:34:F7. The source answer format at `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:330-345`, Figure `fig:ld-decider`, consists of coefficient lists for degree-`d` or degree-`md` univariate polynomials. Defining `deg_md(ℓ)` as functions on the geometric set `ℓ` collapses distinct representatives when the degree is large and collapses every zero-direction parameterization to a single constant function. Consequently the original strategy measurement cannot be indexed as in `def:expanded-line-measurement`, and the universal zero-direction check is lost. Retain parameterized polynomial representatives and explicitly embed degree-`d` ALine outcomes.
results/telemetry/sessions/reviewer-pr0001-20260830-03.last.md:36:F8. The exact last inequality in `lem:povm-to-obs` should be `O(|A|δ)`, and line 869 of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons` should be `O(ε)`. Their approximation conclusions survive after retaining hidden constants, but the displayed proofs do not follow from `def:povm-distance`.
results/telemetry/sessions/reviewer-pr0001-20260830-03.last.md:38:F9. The actual diagonal sampler sets `w=π_{j-1}(v)`, so only coordinates before `j=χ(s)` vanish; `w_j` may vanish and `w=0` has positive probability. Thus line 562's “first nonzero coordinate” assertion is false. Lines 565-570 also choose `s_X,s_Z` without the uniform laws on their `χ`-fibres, while Property 2 mixes distributions on line-point pairs as if they were distributions on lines. Compare `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:230-271` and the inherited defective proof at `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1115`, label `lem:qld-sublines`. A complete conditional sampler and coherent marginal statement are required.
results/telemetry/sessions/reviewer-pr0001-20260830-03.last.md:40:F10. The retained estimate is `O(m(ε^(1/4)+δ_P^(1/4)+δ_Q^(1/4)+δ_Line^(1/2)))`, with `δ_Line=√ε`. Taking `ε=m^-4` and admissible `q` sufficiently large makes both advertised arguments `m²ε` and `md/q` tend to zero while `mε^(1/4)=1`. Hence no vanishing function of the advertised variables dominates the proof. The same mismatch occurs between `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1020-1033`, label `lem:qld-4-13`, and lines 1134-1137. Prove the stronger joint-law route or weaken the error statement.
results/telemetry/sessions/reviewer-pr0001-20260830-03.last.md:42:F11. `def:ld-game` requires its dimension to divide `q`, but `lem:qld-4-7` applies it with dimension `2m+2`. Admissibility gives only `m|q`; for power-of-two `m≥2`, `2m+2=2(m+1)` has an odd factor and cannot divide power-of-two `q`. The source makes the same unsupported application at `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1278-1288`, label `lem:qld-4-7`. The caveat at lines 919-924 documents the gap but does not prove the lemma; a generalized sampler and soundness theorem are needed.
results/telemetry/sessions/reviewer-pr0001-20260830-03.last.md:44:F12. `lem:qld-unitary` controls `V(M_h⊗I)V†`, whereas the defined isometry satisfies `φM_hφ†=V(M_h⊗|EPR⟩⟨EPR|)V†`. The direct inference at lines 281-289, also present at `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1864-1875`, is therefore missing a step. Prove that the difference annihilates the transformed actual state and use projectivity plus its distance from the ideal state to transfer the summed squared estimate.

Complements\nthe lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference, which covers the kernel-level\nblockers; this file covers patterns where the Lean code *compiles and the\ntrick is at the level of what the statement says or what the definitions\nbake in*.\n\nEvery pattern here is **castle-in-the-air in spirit**: a theorem named after a\npaper result that doesn't actually prove it. The named offenders below all\ncross-reference a concrete issue or PR so reviewers can see a real example.\n\n## Why this matters\n\nKernel checks are necessary but not sufficient. A theorem can:\n\n- Be marked `\\leanok` in the blueprint,\n- Have a sorry-free proof body,\n- Have a clean axiom closure (`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` only),\n\nand still prove **nothing that the paper actually claims**, if the proof\nobligation has been displaced into a hypothesis, a definition, or a sentinel\nbranch. The proof body\nis a trivial `rcases`/`exact`/`.trans`/`simpa using h` and does no\nmathematical work. A variant wraps the hypothesis in a named bundle\n(`*BridgePackage`, `*Statement`); see issues [#449], [#451], [#477] for the\ncatalogue, and [#493] for the inline-existential mutation triggered by\nPR [#491].\n\n### Why it's bad\n\nThe theorem's named mathematical content is never derived from prior lemmas;\nthe caller (who supplies the hypothesis) has to discharge it. In practice the\ncaller then has the same problem, pushing the obligation further up the\nstack. The theorem is true under a vacuous hypothesis and the `\\leanok` tag\nmisrepresents the actual state of the proof.\n\n### How to spot it\n\n- The hypothesis type contains, up to `∃` / `∧` / a coercion, the theorem's\n  conclusion.\n- The proof body is one of:\n  - `rcases h with ⟨...⟩; exact ⟨...⟩`\n  - `exact h.fieldName` / `exact h.a.trans h.b`\n  - `by simpa using h.fieldName`\n- The hypothesis is a bundle named `*BridgePackage`, `*Witness`, `*Package`,\n  `*Output`, with a field whose type matches the conclusion structure.\n- Consumers of the bundle are trivial (field projection + return).\n\n### Concrete example\n\nHistorical example (before the MainInductionStep cleanup):\n\n```lean\ntheorem mainInduction\n    (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]\n    (strategy : SymStrat params ι)\n    (eps delta gamma : Error) (k : ℕ)\n    (hbridge : MainInductionBridgePackage params strategy eps delta gamma k) :\n    ∃ G : Measurement (Polynomial params) ι,\n      ConsRel strategy.state ...\n        (mainInductionError params k eps delta gamma) := by\n  rcases hbridge.witness with ⟨error, G, hG, herror⟩\n  refine ⟨G, ?_⟩\n  exact ⟨le_trans hG.offDiagonalBound herror⟩\n```\n\nHere `MainInductionBridgePackage.witness` has type\n`∃ error, ∃ G, ConsRel ... error ∧ error ≤ mainInductionError ...` — literally\nthe conclusion. The code has since been refactored to remove both this\nspecific MainInductionStep bridge and the interim theorem alias that exposed\nthe same witness shape under the paper theorem's name, but the snippet remains\nthe archetypal example of the anti-pattern.\n\nPR [#491] proposed to delete the `*BridgePackage` by **inlining** the bundle's\nfields as explicit hypotheses. That only scatters the same pattern across\nindividual signatures without producing any proof — it's strictly worse\nbecause the named bundle at least shows up in one tracker. Do not accept PRs\nthat discharge an ungrounded bridge by flattening it into conclusion-shaped\nexistential hypotheses, or by reintroducing the same shape under a theorem name\nthat suggests the paper result has been proved.\n\n### How to fix it\n\nPrefer **proving a real intermediate lemma** — one that the paper also uses\n— and stating its signature with the paper's hypotheses (not the theorem's\nconclusion). The \"mathematical\ncontent\" has been baked into the definition; the theorem is a tautology. See\nissues [#477], [#494].\n\n### Why it's bad\n\n`rfl` proves that a definition equals itself. If the definition is chosen\n*so that* it equals the conclusion, the `rfl` \"proof\" transports none of the\npaper's reasoning — it is literally the reflexivity of a shape we invented to\nmatch the conclusion. The Lean theorem states and proves only the trivial fact that the\ndefinition equals itself.\n\n### Not every `rfl` is a castle\n\nDistinguish from legitimate bookkeeping where a named equation is literally\nhow something was defined. Example: `mainFormalError_eq_envelope` in\n`Test/ErrorCascade/Definitions.lean` unfolds the definition of\n`mainFormalError` to its envelope factorization. The mathematical content is\nelsewhere (the envelope is derived from per-step bounds); the `rfl` theorem is\na naming convenience only. The test is: **does the `def` body encode a paper\nidentity, or does it just name a compound expression?**\n\n### How to fix it\n\n1. Move the paper's real definition to the concrete one: for Fourier, define\n   the inner product as the actual sum over vertices, and the characters\n   `φ_α` as functions from `Point params` to `ℂ`.\n2.      2	"""The one GitHub layer for ``local/bin`` — a thin, fail-closed wrapper over ``gh``.
     3	
     4	GitHub is the single source of truth for issues, PRs, CI evidence (commit
     5	statuses on the exact head SHA), review verdicts (COMMENT reviews bound to a
     6	commit id), and merges (REST merge guarded by an exact-SHA match).  This module
     7	is the only place workflow scripts talk to GitHub, as a Python import or via
     8	its CLI (``gh_common.py <subcommand> ...``) from shell.
     9	
    10	Design rules (local/protocols/issues-prs.md):
    11	
    12	* At most one write mutation per invocation of a helper; ambiguity after a
    13	  failed write is resolved by re-reading state and adopting, never by
    14	  repeating the mutation.  Writes that are idempotent by content (statuses,
    15	  close-PATCH) may be retried blindly.
    16	* Everything uses ``gh api`` (raw REST), so no feature of a modern ``gh`` CLI
    17	  is required — the exact-SHA merge guard is the REST ``sha`` parameter, not a
    18	  CLI flag.
    19	* Fail closed: a network failure after retries raises; no local fallback
    20	  record is ever written.
    21	
    22	Environment: ``MIPSTARRE_GH`` (gh binary; default ``gh`` on PATH, then
    23	``~/.local/bin/gh``), ``MIPSTARRE_GITHUB_REPO`` (``owner/repo``; default
    24	parsed from the ``github`` remote of the primary checkout).
    25	"""
    26	
    27	from __future__ import annotations
    28	
    29	import argparse
    30	import json

    41	from wf_util import LayerError, atomic_write, check_bracket_free, default_repo_root, utcnow

    43	#: One page of the REST pagination loop; also the adoption search window.
    44	PAGE = 100
    45	
    46	#: GitHub caps comment/review bodies at 65536 characters; leave headroom for
    47	#: the marker line and the truncation notice.
    48	COMMENT_BODY_LIMIT = 60000
    49	
    50	_TRANSIENT_RE = re.compile(
    51	    r"(?i)(timed? ?out|connection|temporar|unavailable|network|reset by peer|"
    52	    r"tls|eof|http (?:429|5\d\d)|rate limit|bad gateway|service unavailable)"
    53	)
    54	
    55	_REMOTE_RE = re.compile(r"github\.com[:/]([^/]+/[^/\s]+?)(?:\.git)?$")
    56	
    57	
    58	def gh_bin() -> str:
    59	    override = os.environ.get("MIPSTARRE_GH")
    60	    if override:
    61	        return override
    62	    found = shutil.which("gh")
    63	    if found:
    64	        return found
    65	    fallback = Path.home() / ".local" / "bin" / "gh"
    66	    if fallback.exists():
    67	        return str(fallback)
    68	    raise LayerError("gh CLI not found (set MIPSTARRE_GH or install gh)")

    71	def repo_slug(repo_root: Path | None = None) -> str:
    72	    override = os.environ.get("MIPSTARRE_GITHUB_REPO")
    73	    if override:
    74	        return override
    75	    root = repo_root or default_repo_root()
    76	    proc = subprocess.run(
    77	        ["git", "-C", str(root), "remote", "get-url", "github"],
    78	        capture_output=True, text=True,
    79	    )
    80	    if proc.returncode == 0:
    81	        match = _REMOTE_RE.search(proc.stdout.strip())
    82	        if match:
    83	            return match.group(1)
    84	    raise LayerError(
    85	        "cannot resolve the GitHub repo: set MIPSTARRE_GITHUB_REPO=owner/repo "
    86	        "or add a 'github' remote to the primary checkout"
    87	    )

    90	def run_gh(args: list[str], *, input_text: str | None = None,
    91	           mutation: bool = False, idempotent: bool = False,
    92	           retries: int = 3) -> str:
    93	    """Run ``gh`` and return stdout; raise ``LayerError`` on final failure.
    94	
    95	    A non-idempotent mutation is attempted exactly once — the caller owns
    96	    ambiguity recovery by re-reading state.  Reads and idempotent mutations
    97	    retry on transient failures with linear backoff.
    98	    """
    99	    attempts = 1 if (mutation and not idempotent) else max(1, retries)
   100	    env = dict(os.environ, GH_PROMPT_DISABLED="1", GH_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER="1",
   101	               NO_COLOR="1", GH_PAGER="cat")
   102	    last_err = ""
   103	    for attempt in range(1, attempts + 1):
   104	        proc = subprocess.run(
   105	            [gh_bin(), *args], input=input_text,
   106	            capture_output=True, text=True, env=env,
   107	        )
   108	        if proc.returncode == 0:
   109	            return proc.stdout
   110	        last_err = (proc.stderr or proc.stdout or "").strip()
   111	        if attempt < attempts and _TRANSIENT_RE.search(last_err):
   112	            time.sleep(5 * attempt)
   113	            continue
   114	        break
   115	    raise LayerError(f"gh {' '.join(args[:3])}... failed: {last_err[:2000]}")
   116	
   117	
   118	def api(path: str, *, method: str | None = None, payload: dict | None = None,
   119	        paginate: bool = False, mutation: bool = False,
   120	        idempotent: bool = False, absolute: bool = False):
   121	    """Call the REST API under ``repos/<slug>/`` (or an absolute *path*).
   122	
   123	    Pagination is manual (``?per_page=100&page=N``) so nothing here depends on
   124	    a modern ``gh``.  Returns parsed JSON (``None`` for an empty response).
   125	    """
   126	    full = path if absolute else f"repos/{repo_slug()}/{path}"
   127	
   128	    def one(page_path: str):
   129	        args = ["api", page_path]
   130	        if method:
   131	            args += ["-X", method]

   133	        if payload is not None:
   134	            args += ["--input", "-"]

   136	        out = run_gh(args, input_text=input_text, mutation=mutation,
   137	                     idempotent=idempotent)
   138	        return json.loads(out) if out.strip() else None
   139	
   140	    if not paginate:
   141	        return one(full)
   142	
   143	    sep = "&" if "?" in full else "?"
   144	    rows: list = []
   145	    page = 1
   146	    while True:
   147	        batch = one(f"{full}{sep}per_page={PAGE}&page={page}")
   148	        if not batch:
   149	            break
   150	        rows.extend(batch)
   151	        if len(batch) < PAGE:
   152	            break
   153	        page += 1
   154	    return rows
   155	
   156	
   157	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   158	# Commit statuses — CI and review evidence, bound to the exact head SHA
   159	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   160	
   161	def post_status(sha: str, context: str, state: str, description: str = "",
   162	                target_url: str | None = None) -> None:
   163	    """Post one commit status.  Idempotent by content: latest-per-context wins."""
   164	    if state not in ("pending", "success", "failure", "error"):
   165	        raise LayerError(f"invalid status state {state!r}")

   167	               "description": description[:140]}
   168	    if target_url:
   169	        payload["target_url"] = target_url

   171	        mutation=True, idempotent=True)
   172	
   173	
   174	def latest_statuses(sha: str) -> dict[str, dict]:
   175	    """Latest status per context on *sha* (rows arrive newest-first)."""
   176	    rows = api(f"commits/{sha}/statuses", paginate=True)
   177	    latest: dict[str, dict] = {}
   178	    for row in rows:
   179	        context = row.get("context") or ""
   180	        if context and context not in latest:
   181	            latest[context] = {"state": row.get("state"),
   182	                               "description": row.get("description") or "",
   183	                               "created_at": row.get("created_at") or ""}
   184	    return latest
   185	
   186	
   187	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   188	# Pull requests
   189	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   190	
   191	def pr_view(number: int) -> dict:
   192	    return api(f"pulls/{number}")
   193	
   194	
   195	def pr_for_branch(branch: str) -> dict | None:
   196	    """The unique open PR whose head is *branch*, or None."""
   197	    owner = repo_slug().split("/")[0]
   198	    head = urllib.parse.quote(f"{owner}:{branch}", safe=":")
   199	    rows = api(f"pulls?state=open&head={head}", paginate=True)
   200	    if len(rows) > 1:
   201	        raise LayerError(f"multiple open PRs for head {branch!r}")
   202	    return rows[0] if rows else None
   203	
   204	
   205	def ensure_pr_comment(number: int, marker: str, body: str) -> int:
   206	    """Create or update the single PR comment carrying *marker*.
   207	
   208	    The marker (an HTML comment) is the idempotency key: an existing comment
   209	    is PATCHed in place; after an ambiguous POST failure the list is re-read
   210	    and an adopted comment is not re-posted.
   211	    """

   216	            payload={"body": full}, mutation=True, idempotent=True)

   218	    try:
   219	        created = api(f"issues/{number}/comments", method="POST",
   220	                      payload={"body": full}, mutation=True)

   229	def _find_comment(number: int, marker: str) -> int | None:
   230	    for row in api(f"issues/{number}/comments", paginate=True):

   237	    if len(body) > COMMENT_BODY_LIMIT:

   132	_HELD: dict[str, int] = {}

   136	def file_lock(name: str, *, timeout_note: str | None = None) -> Iterator[None]:

   138

   140	    per-entity ``flock`` plus the atomic writer below covers it.  Re-entrant

   177	# Atomic writes
   178	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   179	
   180	def atomic_write(path: Path, text: str) -> None:
   181	    """Write *text* to *path* via tempfile + ``os.replace``.
   182	
   183	    Used for runtime artifacts and telemetry snapshots: a half-written file
   184	    must never be observable.
   185	    """
   186	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   187	    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=str(path.parent), prefix=f".{path.name}.", suffix=".tmp")
   188	    try:
   189	        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
   190	            handle.write(text)
   191	            handle.flush()
   192	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())

   195	        try:
   196	            os.unlink(tmp)
   197	        except OSError:
   198	            pass
   199	        raise
   200	    dir_fd = os.open(str(path.parent), os.O_RDONLY)
   201	    try:
   202	        os.fsync(dir_fd)
   203	    finally:
   204	        os.close(dir_fd)

     6	issues, PRs, CI and review evidence, and merges; CI and reviews still *execute*
     7	here and publish their results there. No active `issues/` or `prs/` tree, no
     8	shadow record, no write-through cache, no offline mutation mode: a GitHub error
     9	fails the operation, never a local success (EVOLUTION.md 2026-09-01).
    10	
    11	## 1. Records, names, tools
    12	
    13	Issues and PRs are GitHub's, identified by their numbers — no zero-padded ids,
    14	no frontmatter. Parent/child structure is the native sub-issue relation
    15	(`POST …/issues/{parent}/sub_issues`), one parent per issue exactly as the
    16	retired `parent:` scalar allowed; discussion is comments; labels come from the
    17	repository (`list-labels`, paginated), so `local/labels.yml` is retired and a
    18	label absent from GitHub is reported, never invented. Briefs (the design record
    19	per issue) live in `local/briefs/`: agent input, not lifecycle state.
    20	
    21	Every GitHub call goes through `local/bin/gh_common.py` — a module for Python
    22	callers, and for the shell scripts a CLI (`pr-view`, `post-status`,
    23	`latest-statuses`, `ensure-pr-comment`, `post-review`, `merge-pr`,
    24	`issue-create`, `issue-close`, `snapshot`, …; `--help` lists them) owning CLI
    25	discovery, repository resolution, API version headers, bounded retry of
    26	transient failures and the exit-2-with-stderr convention. Nothing else shells
    27	out to `gh`. `issue_new.py`, `issue_close.py`, `pr_open.py`, `ci.sh`,
    28	`review.sh`, `autofix.sh`, `pr_merge.py`, `github-sync.sh` take GitHub numbers;
    29	`track.py`, `validate_tree.py` and `export_issues.py` are deleted.
    30	
    31	* Branches: `issue-<github-number>-<slug>`, or `codex/issue-<number>-<slug>`
    32	  from an agent; `pr_open.py` rejects what `git check-ref-format` would.
    33	* Titles, slugs and branch names are **bracket-free**: bot-generated branch
    34	  names inherit those characters and "`]` breaks part of the PR automation
    35	  stack" (docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124). A `:` in a *title* is fine
    36	  (`Tracking: …`), but not in a branch.
    37	* Fix commits keep the exact subject prefixes `[codex-auto-fix]` and
    38	  `[codex-review-fix]`; the iteration counter and the review skip key on them.
    39	* `Closes #N` / `Fixes #N` auto-closes the issue on merge, `Addresses #N` does
    40	  not (docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:61-62) — and the numbers being GitHub's, that
    41	  footer is now literally what GitHub itself reads.
    42	
    43	## 2. Evidence contracts
    44	
    45	All evidence binds to the **exact head SHA** (DESIGN.md invariant 2).
    46	
    47	**Commit statuses.** Ten canonical contexts, posted by `post-status`: one
    48	`local-ci/<step>` per CI step (`build`, `blueprint-render`, `paper-gaps`,
    49	`blueprint-sync`, `file-length`, `proof-debt`, `proof-evasion`,
    50	`statement-origin`), plus `local-ci/summary` and `local-review/summary`.
    51	`ci.sh` posts `pending` before each gate step and `success | failure | error`
    52	after it; a gated-out step is a `success` saying it was skipped. The gate reads
    53	the *latest* status per context (`latest-statuses`), never GitHub's combined
    54	status, silent as that is about contexts never posted. The run manifest is one
    55	PR comment marked `<!-- mipstarre-ci-manifest pr=N -->`, kept current by
    56	`ensure-pr-comment`: evidence for humans, while the statuses are the gate.
    57	
    58	**Review verdict.** One `COMMENT` review per head SHA, bound to `commit_id`,
    59	carrying `<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->`, the findings ledger, and the
    60	line `VERDICT: APPROVED | COMMENTED | CHANGES_REQUESTED (code=…, prose=…)`.
    61	Unchecked findings are ledger lines matching `^\s*[-*]\s*\[ \]`; clean means
    62	`APPROVED`, or `COMMENTED` with none of them. Adverse verdicts post as `COMMENT`
    63	too — a **single account** cannot approve its own pull request, so the review
    64	event carries no authority — and adverseness travels in `local-review/summary`
    65	(`failure` for unresolved findings), which is the gate's review evidence.
    66	
    67	**Adjudication** (review.md §12) is a PR comment whose body starts with
    68	`ADJUDICATION` and contains `head=<SHA>` for the current head, one disposition
    69	line per remaining finding; `--adjudicated` takes nothing else.
    70	
    71	**Idempotency.** Every publishing step is **at most one mutation**: a paginated
    72	read finds the stable marker first and adopts that record instead of duplicating
    73	it (`commentOnce`, issue-automation.yml:403-417, now guarding retries rather than
    74	webhook redelivery); an ambiguous write stays pending for adoption.
    75	
    76	## 3. The merge gate
    77	
    78	`pr_merge.py <number>` is the only path to `main`: never `git merge` to main,
    79	never push `main`. The merge is a REST `PUT …/pulls/{n}/merge` with the exact
    80	`sha` guard, issued by `gh_common.merge_pr` and verified against the merge
    81	commit's topology (two parents, the frozen head second), behind seven gates
    82	that refuse by default:
    83	
    84	1. the PR is open, unmerged and not a draft (`draft is False`, not merely
    85	   falsy), and reports a head SHA, a head ref and a base ref;
    86	2. the primary worktree is clean and on the base, and the local branch tip
    87	   equals the GitHub head SHA — the merge must be of the bytes built here;
    88	3. all eight `local-ci/<step>` contexts plus `local-ci/summary` are `success` on
    89	   that exact SHA; a **missing** context blocks, because GitHub's combined state
    90	   reads `success` for a commit carrying no statuses at all;
    91	4. that SHA's marker-bound `COMMENT` review carries `VERDICT: APPROVED`, or
    92	   `COMMENTED` with zero unchecked findings, **and** `local-review/summary` is
    93	   `success` there;
    94	5. no `CHANGES_REQUESTED` review stands on that head, from anyone;
    95	6. no live fix lock for the branch (`locks/fix-<branch>.lock`, running holder),
    96	   and the fix-iteration count — `merge-base..head` commits whose subject starts
    97	   with a §1 fix prefix — is within `MIPSTARRE_FIX_CAP`;
    98	7. every issue the PR body closes — all nine of GitHub's closing keywords, not
    99	   just `Closes` — has no open sub-issue left.
   100	
   101	`--adjudicated` waives gate 4's adverse verdict and nothing else, and only when
   102	an exact-head `ADJUDICATION` comment backs it; gate 5 is never adjudicable.
   103	
   104	Afterwards a best-effort, non-fatal tail fast-forwards local `main` to the
   105	remote merge commit; branch and worktree cleanup keeps its safeguards (local
   106	dirt defers it with a warning).
   107	
   108	## 4. Untrusted text
   109	
   110	Issue and PR bodies are untrusted data, and **more** so now that they arrive
   111	from GitHub: anyone with repository access, and every imported external report,
   112	writes the fields that are echoed into generated markdown and interpolated into
   113	agent prompts. All three parent workflows sanitized before interpolation, and
   114	`wf_util.sanitize` is that step ported: strip control characters, break fenced
   115	code with zero-width spaces, truncate to 200 characters for titles and 5000 for
   116	bodies (issue-automation.yml:122-128).
   117	
   118	Every LLM hook in `local/bin` carries the same four requirements: gate on
   119	`MIPSTARRE_LLM_ENABLED != "false"`; read prompts from committed main
   120	(`git show main:…`), never the branch under review (DESIGN.md:76-77); frame
   121	sanitized text as data that must not be followed; and filter any model-proposed
   122	label through the repository's label list. `audit_stale_issues.py` additionally
   123	keeps its path-traversal rejection for externally sourced citations.
   124	
   125	## 5. Environment, snapshot, archive
   126	
   127	`MIPSTARRE_GH` is the path to `gh` (else `PATH`, else the documented user-local
   128	location); `MIPSTARRE_GITHUB_REPO` overrides the `owner/name` otherwise read
   129	from the `github` remote; `MIPSTARRE_FIX_CAP` is the combined fix-iteration cap,
   130	default 5 — the old table's `MIPSTARRE_FIX_ITERATION_CAP` row was wrong, the
   131	code reads `MIPSTARRE_FIX_CAP`. `MIPSTARRE_LLM_ENABLED` and
   132	`LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED` keep kill-switch semantics (DESIGN.md:73-75).
   133	
   134	`github-sync.sh` pushes explicit refs and writes an atomic, paginated read-only
   135	snapshot of open issues and PRs to `results/telemetry/github-snapshot/`
   136	(`open-issues.json`, `open-pulls.json`, `metadata.json`; PRs filtered out of the
   137	issue endpoint) — audit and recovery telemetry, never lifecycle input. The
   138	retired trees stay archived under `results/telemetry/registry-archive/` (commit
   139	c8f1999): read-only research data, never edited or read as active input.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""The merge gate: prove the exact head SHA is green and reviewed, then merge it.
     3	
     4	The one script in the issue-lifecycle area that changes ``main``: the local
     5	replacement for GitHub's branch-protection rules, which upstream were server-side
     6	settings no client could bypass.  A single-account repository has none — the owner can
     7	always press Merge — so the authority is this file.  It refuses by default, every
     8	override is named, and ``gh_common.merge_pr`` merges through the REST ``sha`` guard,
     9	which makes GitHub reject the call if the head moved meanwhile.
    10	
    11	Every piece of evidence lives on GitHub, bound to the head SHA (issues-prs.md; the old
    12	``prs/`` registry is archived under ``results/telemetry/registry-archive/``):
    13	
    14	1. the PR is open, unmerged, not a draft;
    15	2. the primary worktree is clean and on the base, and the local branch tip is that
    16	   SHA — the merge must be of the bytes that were built here;
    17	3. the eight ``local-ci/<step>`` contexts (ci.sh:70) and ``local-ci/summary`` are
    18	   ``success`` on it.  A missing context blocks: GitHub's combined state reads
    19	   "success" for a commit carrying no statuses at all;
    20	4. a ``<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->`` COMMENT review sits on that exact
    21	   commit id, its ``VERDICT:`` line is APPROVED (or COMMENTED with zero unchecked
    22	   findings), and ``local-review/summary`` is ``success`` (DESIGN.md:66-69) — one
    23	   account cannot self-APPROVE, so an adverse verdict travels in that status;
    24	5. no ``CHANGES_REQUESTED`` review sits on that SHA, from anyone;
    25	6. the fix loop is quiescent: no live autofix.sh lock, and the ``[codex-auto-fix]``
    26	   / ``[codex-review-fix]`` commits since the merge base are within the cap;
    27	7. every issue this PR closes has no open sub-issue left.
    28	
    29	``--adjudicated`` waives gate 4's adverse verdict — nothing else — when an
    30	``ADJUDICATION`` comment names this exact head (review.md 12).  GitHub merges and
    31	closes the linked issues itself, so no local bookkeeping can double-count.  The
    32	best-effort tail then fast-forwards local ``main``, refreshes the
    33	``refs/remotes/origin/main`` alias the hooks and diff-based audits need in order not
    34	to self-disable (DESIGN.md:83-85), warms the cache and drops the branch.
    35	
    36	Usage: pr_merge.py N [--check-only | --dry-run] [--adjudicated] [--no-warm-cache]

    83	def git(repo_root: Path, *args: str, check: bool = True) -> str:
    84	    result = subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=str(repo_root),
    85	                            capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)

    87	        raise LayerError(f"git {' '.join(args)} failed ({result.returncode}): "
    88	                         f"{result.stderr.strip() or result.stdout.strip()}")
    89	    return result.stdout.strip()

   114	def ensure_mergeable_worktree(repo_root: Path, branch: str, base: str, head_sha: str) -> None:
   115	    """Gate 2 — clean primary worktree on the base, local branch at the head.
   116	
   117	    GitHub performs the merge, so none of this is needed for the merge itself; all of it
   118	    is needed for the tail, which fast-forwards ``base`` in this very worktree and
   119	    deletes the branch.  Refusing here keeps the failure before the irreversible step.
   120	    """
   121	    dirty = git(repo_root, "status", "--porcelain")
   122	    if dirty:
   123	        raise GateFailure("gate 2 (worktree): the primary tree is not clean, required clean "
   124	                          "so the post-merge fast-forward cannot lose work:\n" + dirty)
   125	    current = git(repo_root, "rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD")
   126	    if current != base:
   127	        raise GateFailure(f"gate 2 (worktree): HEAD is on {current!r}, required {base!r} "
   128	                          f"(the PR base). Run: git switch {base}")
   129	    tip = git(repo_root, "rev-parse", "--verify", f"{branch}^{{commit}}", check=False)
   130	    if not tip:
   131	        raise GateFailure(f"gate 2 (local branch): {branch!r} does not resolve here, required "
   132	                          f"it at {head_sha[:12]}: git fetch github {branch}:{branch}")
   133	    if tip != head_sha:
   134	        raise GateFailure(f"gate 2 (local branch): {branch} tip is {tip[:12]}, required "
   135	                          f"{head_sha[:12]} (the PR head). Push or fetch — the evidence binds "
   136	                          "to the SHA, not to the branch name.")
   137	    passed(f"gate 2 worktree clean on {base}, local tip == head")

   140	def check_ci(statuses: dict, head_sha: str) -> None:
   141	    """Gate 3 — every CI context is ``success`` on the exact head SHA."""
   142	    problems: list[str] = []
   143	    for context in CI_CONTEXTS:
   144	        row = statuses.get(context)
   145	        if row is None:
   146	            problems.append(f"{context}: MISSING")
   147	        elif row.get("state") != "success":
   148	            problems.append(f"{context}: {row.get('state')} "
   149	                            f"({sanitize(str(row.get('description') or ''), 120)})")
   150	    if problems:
   151	        raise GateFailure(f"gate 3 (CI): required success on {head_sha[:12]} for all "
   152	                          f"{len(CI_CONTEXTS)} contexts; observed:\n  " + "\n  ".join(problems)
   153	                          + "\nRun local/bin/ci.sh on this head. A missing context is a block, "
   154	                          "never a pass: GitHub's combined state is 'success' for a commit "
   155	                          "with no statuses at all.")
   156	    passed(f"gate 3 all {len(CI_CONTEXTS)} local-ci contexts success")

   159	def check_review(number: int, head_sha: str, reviews: list[dict], statuses: dict,
   160	                 *, adjudicated: bool) -> None:
   161	    """Gate 4 — one verdict review on this commit id, clean or adjudicated."""
   162	    marker = f"<!-- mipstarre-review pr={number} head={head_sha} -->"
   163	    matching = [r for r in reviews
   164	                if r.get("commit_id") == head_sha and marker in (r.get("body") or "")]
   165	    if not matching:
   166	        raise GateFailure(f"gate 4 (review): no review carrying {marker} on commit "
   167	                          f"{head_sha[:12]}, required exactly one. A verdict on an earlier SHA "
   168	                          "does not carry over (DESIGN.md:66-69): re-run review.sh.")
   169	    # One verdict review per head is the contract; if a retry ever leaves two, the newest
   170	    # is operative (the API returns reviews in creation order).
   171	    body = matching[-1].get("body") or ""
   172	    found = VERDICT_RE.search(body)
   173	    verdict = found.group(1) if found else ""
   174	    unchecked = len(UNCHECKED_FINDING_RE.findall(body))
   175	    summary_state = (statuses.get(REVIEW_CONTEXT) or {}).get("state")
   176	    # Green needs BOTH a clean verdict and a clean ledger: an APPROVED trailer
   177	    # over unresolved findings is inconsistent reviewer output (round 2, F4).
   178	    clean = verdict in ("APPROVED", "COMMENTED") and unchecked == 0
   179	    if clean and summary_state == "success":
   180	        passed(f"gate 4 verdict {verdict} on {head_sha[:12]}, {REVIEW_CONTEXT} success")
   181	        return
   182	    observed = (f"VERDICT {verdict or 'absent'} with {unchecked} unchecked finding(s), "
   183	                f"{REVIEW_CONTEXT} {summary_state or 'MISSING'}")
   184	    if not adjudicated:
   185	        raise GateFailure(f"gate 4 (review): required VERDICT APPROVED, or COMMENTED with zero "
   186	                          f"unchecked findings, and {REVIEW_CONTEXT} success; observed "
   187	                          f"{observed}. Address the findings (or tick them off with a reason and "
   188	                          "a tracked issue) and re-run review.sh, or merge --adjudicated.")
   189	    # review.md section 12: past the round cap the operator may adjudicate what is left.
   190	    # Binding the comment to the SHA stops an adjudication of round four covering five.
   191	    where = None
   192	    for row in gh_common.api(f"issues/{number}/comments", paginate=True):
   193	        text = (row.get("body") or "").lstrip()
   194	        if text.startswith("ADJUDICATION") and f"head={head_sha}" in text:
   195	            where = str(row.get("html_url") or row.get("id"))
   196	            break
   197	    if where is None:
   198	        raise GateFailure(f"gate 4 (review): --adjudicated given but no ADJUDICATION comment "
   199	                          f"names head={head_sha} on PR #{number}; observed {observed}. Post one "
   200	                          f"first: a comment starting with ADJUDICATION, containing that head.")
   201	    sys.stderr.write(f"warning: merging PR #{number} on operator adjudication ({where}); the "
   202	                     f"review evidence is adverse — {observed}\n")
   203	    passed(f"gate 4 adjudicated at {head_sha[:12]} ({where})")

   206	def check_fix_gates(repo_root: Path, branch: str, base: str, head_sha: str) -> str:
   207	    """Gate 6 — refuse while the serialized fix loop is mid-flight or over its cap.
   208	    Returns the merge base (gate 7 scans the same commit range)."""
   209	    # autofix.sh holds a mkdir-based lease keyed on the BRANCH (autofix.sh:580,
   210	    # locks/fix-<branch with / -> ->.lock, holder pid in <lock>/pid).  Probe the same lock
   211	    # the same way; a dead holder's lock does not block the merge.
   212	    lock = lock_dir() / ("fix-" + branch.replace("/", "-") + ".lock")
   213	    if lock.is_dir():
   214	        pid_text = ""
   215	        try:
   216	            pid_text = (lock / "pid").read_text(encoding="ascii").split()[0]
   217	        except (OSError, IndexError):
   218	            pass
   219	        if pid_text.isdigit() and _pid_alive(int(pid_text)):
   220	            raise GateFailure(f"gate 6 (fix loop): {lock} is held by live pid {pid_text}, required "
   221	                              "idle. autofix.sh is rewriting this branch and merging under it "
   222	                              "would race the fix commits.")
   223	    base_ref = None
   224	    for candidate in (f"github/{base}", f"refs/remotes/origin/{base}", base):
   225	        if git_ok(repo_root, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", f"{candidate}^{{commit}}"):
   226	            base_ref = candidate
   227	            break
   228	    if base_ref is None:
   229	        raise GateFailure(f"gate 6 (fix cap): no local ref resolves for base {base!r}, so the "
   230	                          f"fix iterations cannot be counted. Run: git fetch github {base}")
   231	    merge_base = git(repo_root, "merge-base", base_ref, head_sha)
   232	    # `git rev-list --format` prints a "commit <sha>" header before each formatted line.
   233	    lines = git(repo_root, "rev-list", "--format=%s", f"{merge_base}..{head_sha}").splitlines()
   234	    iterations = sum(1 for line in lines if not line.startswith("commit ")
   235	                     and line.startswith(FIX_COMMIT_PREFIXES))
   236	    cap = int(os.environ.get("MIPSTARRE_FIX_CAP", DEFAULT_FIX_CAP))
   237	    if iterations > cap:
   238	        raise GateFailure(f"gate 6 (fix cap): {iterations} fix commit(s) on {branch} since "
   239	                          f"{merge_base[:12]}, required at most {cap}. The cap is combined across "
   240	                          "ci/blueprint/review fixes (DESIGN.md:70-72); a PR past it needs human "
   241	                          "attention, not another merge attempt.")
   242	    passed(f"gate 6 fix loop idle, {iterations}/{cap} fix commits")
   243	    return merge_base

   246	def check_dependencies(repo_root: Path, number: int, body: str,
   247	                       merge_base: str, head_sha: str) -> None:

   249	
   250	    GitHub honors closing keywords in the PR body AND in commit messages that

   252	    ``owner/repo#N`` references are out of scope: single-repo project.)

   256	                        check=False))
   257	    closes = list(dict.fromkeys(n for text in surfaces
   258	                                for n in CLOSES_RE.findall(text)))

261	        if children:

     6	archived read-only under ``results/telemetry/registry-archive/``).  Only the
     7	pieces with no registry coupling live here: runtime locations, untrusted-text
     8	sanitization, naming rules, the per-entity advisory lock, and the atomic

    41	#: structural reason — a name that travels through shell, path and regex
    42	#: contexts must survive all three.
    43	FORBIDDEN_REF_CHARS = "[]~^:?*\\ \t"

    50

    54

    81	    """Strip control characters, break ``` fences, optionally truncate.
    82	
    83	    Verbatim port of the ``Sanitize issue content`` step at
    84	    ``.github/workflows/issue-automation.yml:122-128``.  Issue and PR text is
    85	    untrusted even when it originates locally — and doubly so now that bodies
    86	    round-trip through GitHub, where anyone with repo read access can quote
    87	    them.  Fence-breaking inserts zero-width spaces so a body cannot close a
    88	    fenced block that frames it as data.

   138	
   139	    The hazard is two agent sessions mutating the same runtime state; a
   140	    per-entity ``flock`` plus the atomic writer below covers it.  Re-entrant
   141	    within one process so a caller may hold a lock while a helper re-acquires
   142	    it.

   144	    if _HELD.get(name):
   145	        _HELD[name] += 1
   146	        try:
   147	            yield
   148	        finally:
   149	            _HELD[name] -= 1
   150	        return

   152	    directory = lock_dir()

   155	    fd = os.open(str(path), os.O_CREAT | os.O_RDWR, 0o644)
   156	    try:
   157	        try:
   158	            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
   159	        except OSError as exc:

   181	    """Write *text* to *path* via tempfile + ``os.replace``.
   182	
   183	    Used for runtime artifacts and telemetry snapshots: a half-written file
   184	    must never be observable.

   568	  warn "worktree $WORKTREE is on '$_wt_branch' but PR #$PR_ID's head branch is '$BRANCH'"
   569	fi
   570	
   571	HEAD_SHA="$(git -C "$WORKTREE" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)"
   572	[ -n "$HEAD_SHA" ] || die "$WORKTREE has no commits to test"
   573	
   574	# Invariant 8: origin/main must resolve.  The diff-based audits and the change
   575	# gating below silently self-disable without a base, which is exactly the
   576	# "checks stopped running and nobody noticed" failure the parent repo hit.
   577	BASE_REF=""
   578	for _cand in "origin/$BASE" "$BASE"; do
   579	  if git -C "$WORKTREE" rev-parse --verify --quiet "$_cand^{commit}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   580	    BASE_REF="$_cand"
   581	    break
   582	  fi
   583	done
   584	[ -n "$BASE_REF" ] || die "neither origin/$BASE nor $BASE resolves in $WORKTREE; local convention is a main branch plus a refs/remotes/origin/main alias maintained by pr_merge.py (DESIGN.md invariant 8)"
   585	
   586	MERGE_BASE="$(git -C "$WORKTREE" merge-base "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_SHA" 2>/dev/null || true)"
   587	[ -n "$MERGE_BASE" ] || die "no merge base between $BASE_REF and $HEAD_SHA"
   588	
   589	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   590	# Change detection and per-area gating
   591	#
   592	# These globs MUST stay in lockstep with the dorny/paths-filter block in
   593	# .github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:83-113 and with the trees the audit scripts
   594	# scan.  The parent repo patched those filters twice after checks silently
   595	# never ran; see local/protocols/ci.md, "Gating globs".
   596	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   597	
   598	CHANGED_FILES="$RUN_TMP/changed-files.txt"
   599	# --no-renames: report both the old and the new path so a rename out of a
   600	# gated tree still trips that tree's filter.  Deletions count too.
   601	git -C "$WORKTREE" diff --name-only --no-renames "$MERGE_BASE" "$HEAD_SHA" > "$CHANGED_FILES"
   602	
   603	A_lean=0
   604	A_mip_lean=0
   605	A_ldt_lean=0
   606	A_blueprint=0
   607	A_blueprint_src=0
   608	A_tex_chapter=0
   609	A_paper_gaps=0
   610	A_scripts=0
   611	A_comparator=0
   612	A_workflow=0
   613	
   614	match_globs() {
   615	  # $1 = path, $2.. = fnmatch patterns ('*' spans '/', as in minimatch '**')
   616	  local _path="$1" _pattern
   617	  shift
   618	  for _pattern in "$@"; do
   619	    # shellcheck disable=SC2254  # unquoted on purpose: $_pattern IS the glob
   620	    case "$_path" in
   621	      $_pattern) return 0 ;;
   622	    esac
   623	  done
   624	  return 1
   625	}
   626	
   627	while IFS= read -r _file; do
   628	  [ -n "$_file" ] || continue
   629	  if match_globs "$_file" '*.lean' 'lakefile.*' 'lean-toolchain' 'lake-manifest.json'; then A_lean=1; fi
   630	  if match_globs "$_file" 'MIPStarRE/*.lean'; then A_mip_lean=1; fi
   631	  if match_globs "$_file" 'MIPStarRE/LDT/*.lean'; then A_ldt_lean=1; fi
   632	  if match_globs "$_file" 'blueprint/*'; then A_blueprint=1; fi
   633	  if match_globs "$_file" 'blueprint/src/*'; then A_blueprint_src=1; fi
   634	  if match_globs "$_file" 'blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex'; then A_tex_chapter=1; fi
   635	  if match_globs "$_file" 'docs/paper-gaps/*' 'texra-blueprint.toml' 'MIPStarRE/*.lean' 'blueprint/src/*' 'docs/*.md'; then A_paper_gaps=1; fi
   636	  if match_globs "$_file" 'scripts/*'; then A_scripts=1; fi
   637	  if match_globs "$_file" 'scripts/comparator/*'; then A_comparator=1; fi
   638	  # 'workflow' is the local translation of "the CI definition itself changed".
   639	  # It covers the WHOLE workflow layer, not just this driver: any local/bin or
   640	  # hook change must trigger every step, including the unit suite that tests it
   641	  # (PR 7 review, F13 — a gh_common.py-only change previously ran nothing).
   642	  if match_globs "$_file" '.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml' 'local/bin/*' \
   643	      'local/protocols/*' '.githooks/*'; then A_workflow=1; fi
   644	done < "$CHANGED_FILES"
   645	
   646	step_gate() {
   647	  case "$1" in
   648	    build)            [ "$A_lean" = 1 ] || [ "$A_comparator" = 1 ] || [ "$A_workflow" = 1 ] ;;
   649	    blueprint-render) [ "$A_blueprint_src" = 1 ] || [ "$A_workflow" = 1 ] ;;
   650	    paper-gaps)       [ "$A_paper_gaps" = 1 ] || [ "$A_workflow" = 1 ] ;;
   651	    blueprint-sync)   [ "$A_lean" = 1 ] || [ "$A_blueprint" = 1 ] || [ "$A_scripts" = 1 ] || [ "$A_workflow" = 1 ] ;;
   652	    file-length)      [ "$A_mip_lean" = 1 ] || [ "$A_scripts" = 1 ] || [ "$A_workflow" = 1 ] ;;
   653	    proof-debt)       [ "$A_mip_lean" = 1 ] || [ "$A_tex_chapter" = 1 ] || [ "$A_scripts" = 1 ] || [ "$A_workflow" = 1 ] ;;
   654	    proof-evasion)    [ "$A_mip_lean" = 1 ] || [ "$A_scripts" = 1 ] || [ "$A_workflow" = 1 ] ;;
   655	    statement-origin) [ "$A_ldt_lean" = 1 ] || [ "$A_scripts" = 1 ] || [ "$A_workflow" = 1 ] ;;
   656	    *) return 1 ;;
   657	  esac
   658	}
   659	
   660	step_gate_paths() {
   661	  case "$1" in
   662	    build)            printf 'lean|comparator|workflow\n' ;;
   663	    blueprint-render) printf 'blueprint_src|workflow\n' ;;
   664	    paper-gaps)       printf 'paper_gaps|workflow\n' ;;
   665	    blueprint-sync)   printf 'lean|blueprint|scripts|workflow\n' ;;
   666	    file-length)      printf 'mip_lean|scripts|workflow\n' ;;
   667	    proof-debt)       printf 'mip_lean|tex_chapter|scripts|workflow\n' ;;
   668	    proof-evasion)    printf 'mip_lean|scripts|workflow\n' ;;
   669	    statement-origin) printf 'ldt_lean|scripts|workflow\n' ;;
   670	  esac
   671	}
   672	
   673	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   674	# Run bookkeeping
   675	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   676	
   677	LOG_DIR="$CACHE_ROOT/ci-logs/$PR_ID/$HEAD_SHA"
   678	
   679	# A run that was told to skip jobs cannot produce a merge-gate verdict.  It
   680	# writes a clearly-named side manifest and posts nothing at all, so a debugging
   681	# --only run can never leave the review gate a green status it did not earn.
   682	PARTIAL=0
   683	if [ -n "$ONLY_STEPS" ] || [ "$SKIP_BUILD" = 1 ] || [ -n "$BASE_OVERRIDE" ]; then
   684	  # --base is in this list because an overridden base (the PR head, say) can
   685	  # empty the diff and mark every gate skipped-success (round 2 F1; round 3 F1
   686	  # caught this line resetting the earlier fix).
   687	  PARTIAL=1
   688	fi
   689	# The manifest is runtime evidence, not a record: GitHub carries the verdict
   690	# (statuses + the manifest comment), the cache carries the raw JSON next to
   691	# the step logs it references.
   692	MANIFEST_DIR="$CACHE_ROOT/ci-manifests"
   693	if [ "$PARTIAL" = 1 ]; then
   694	  MANIFEST="$MANIFEST_DIR/pr$PR_ID-$HEAD_SHA.partial.json"
   695	else
   696	  MANIFEST="$MANIFEST_DIR/pr$PR_ID-$HEAD_SHA.json"
   697	fi
   698	STEPS_TSV="$RUN_TMP/steps.tsv"
   699	WARN_FILE="$RUN_TMP/warnings.txt"
   700	: > "$STEPS_TSV"
   701	: > "$WARN_FILE"
   702	
   703	sanitize_field() {
   704	  printf '%s' "$1" | tr '\t\n\r' '   ' | cut -c1-500
   705	}
   706	
   707	record_step() {
   708	  # name outcome seconds log blocking note
   709	  printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
   710	    "$1" "$2" "$3" "$4" "$5" "$(sanitize_field "${6:-}")" >> "$STEPS_TSV"
   711	}
   712	
   713	SHORT_SHA="$(git -C "$WORKTREE" rev-parse --short "$HEAD_SHA")"
   714	info "PR $PR_ID  branch $BRANCH  head $SHORT_SHA  base $BASE_REF"
   715	info "worktree $WORKTREE"
   716	info "changed files: $(wc -l < "$CHANGED_FILES" | tr -d ' ')"
   717	info "areas: lean=$A_lean mip_lean=$A_mip_lean ldt_lean=$A_ldt_lean blueprint=$A_blueprint blueprint_src=$A_blueprint_src tex_chapter=$A_tex_chapter paper_gaps=$A_paper_gaps scripts=$A_scripts comparator=$A_comparator workflow=$A_workflow"
   718	
   719	if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
   720	  info "dry run: planned steps"
   721	  for _step in $STEP_NAMES; do
   722	    _plan="skip"
   723	    if [ "$FORCE_ALL" = 1 ] || step_gate "$_step"; then _plan="run"; fi
   724	    if [ -n "$ONLY_STEPS" ]; then
   725	      case " $ONLY_STEPS " in
   726	        *" $_step "*) ;;
   727	        *) _plan="skip (--only)" ;;
   728	      esac
   729	    fi
   730	    if [ "$_step" = build ] && [ "$SKIP_BUILD" = 1 ]; then _plan="skip (--skip-build)"; fi
   731	    printf '  %-18s %s\n' "$_step" "$_plan"
   732	  done
   733	  info "manifest would be $MANIFEST"
   734	  info "dry run: no commit statuses and no PR comment are posted"
   735	  exit 0
   736	fi
   737	
   738	# Per-PR serialization.  A second run for the same PR is refused rather than
   739	# cancelling the first: the parent workflow only cancels in-progress PR runs
   740	# because the runner is disposable; locally a killed run leaves a half-built
   741	# .lake/build and a half-held build lock behind (gotcha 5).
   742	PR_LOCK="$CACHE_ROOT/locks/ci-$PR_ID.lock"
   743	if ! acquire_lock "$PR_LOCK" 0 "$BUILD_LOCK_STALE_S" "ci.sh pr=$PR_ID sha=$HEAD_SHA"; then
   744	  die "another ci.sh run for PR $PR_ID is in progress (lock $PR_LOCK, pid $(head -n 1 "$PR_LOCK/owner" 2>/dev/null || echo '?')); wait for it or break the lock by hand"
   745	fi
   746	
   747	mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR" "$MANIFEST_DIR"
   748	
   749	# Every status this run writes is bound to the SHA it actually tested; a status
   750	# that cannot be written is fatal, because GitHub is the only CI record and a
   751	# local fallback would be evidence nobody can trust.
   752	post_status() {
   753	  # sha context state [description]
   754	  python3 "$GH_COMMON" post-status "$1" "$2" "$3" --desc "${4:-}" \
   755	    || die "could not post $2=$3 on $1 (GitHub is the only CI record; refusing to invent a local one)"
   756	}
   757	
   758	# Mark every step pending before anything can fail: a crashed run must never
   759	# leave a stale `success` behind for the review or merge gate to trust.
   760	if [ "$PARTIAL" = 1 ]; then
   761	  info "partial run (--only/--skip-build): no commit statuses and no manifest comment; the manifest goes to $(basename "$MANIFEST")"
   762	else
   763	  [ "$HEAD_SHA" = "$GH_HEAD_SHA" ] || die "worktree head $HEAD_SHA is not PR #$PR_ID's head $GH_HEAD_SHA; push the branch (local/bin/github-sync.sh) or check out the pushed commit — CI evidence is only ever bound to the SHA GitHub knows"
   764	  # The bytes must BE the SHA: a dirty worktree would let uncommitted repairs
   765	  # pass CI for code GitHub has never seen (PR 7 review, F1).
   766	  DIRTY="$(git -C "$WORKTREE" status --porcelain)"
   767	  [ -z "$DIRTY" ] || die "worktree $WORKTREE is dirty; commit or stash before a publishing CI run:
   768	$DIRTY"
   769	  # Invalidate the previous roll-up first so nothing can read a stale green
   770	  # summary while this run is in flight (PR 7 review, F3).
   771	  post_status "$HEAD_SHA" "local-ci/summary" pending "rerun in progress (local/bin/ci.sh)"
   772	  for _step in $STEP_NAMES; do
   773	    post_status "$HEAD_SHA" "local-ci/$_step" pending "queued by local/bin/ci.sh"
   774	  done
   775	  info "posted pending local-ci/* statuses (summary + 8 steps) on $SHORT_SHA"
   776	fi
   777	
   778	RUN_STARTED="$(iso_now)"
   779	RUN_START_EPOCH="$(epoch_now)"
   780	
   781	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   782	# Step bodies.  Each runs in a subshell with cwd = the branch worktree, stdout
   783	# and stderr redirected to its log.  Exit 0 = pass, EXIT_TOOL_MISSING = the
   784	# step could not run at all, anything else = a real failure.
   785	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   786	
   787	note_warning() { printf '%s\n' "$*" >> "$WARN_FILE"; printf 'WARNING: %s\n' "$*"; }
   788	
   789	require_tool() {
   790	  # $1 = executable, $2 = how to install it
   791	  if command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   792	    return 0
   793	  fi
   794	  printf 'ERROR: required tool %s is not on PATH.\n' "$1"
   795	  printf 'Install it with: %s\n' "$2"
   796	  exit "$EXIT_TOOL_MISSING"
   797	}
   798	
   799	step_build() {
   800	  cd "$WORKTREE"
   801	
   802	  # Warm .lake/build from the hot main snapshot before compiling.  The warmer
   803	  # is the only writer of the shared snapshot; this worktree gets a private
   804	  # copy-on-write clone (DESIGN.md invariant 1).
   805	  if [ ! -d .lake/build ]; then
   806	    if [ -x "$SCRIPT_DIR/warm-worktree.sh" ]; then
   807	      echo "+ warm-worktree.sh $WORKTREE"
   808	      if ! "$SCRIPT_DIR/warm-worktree.sh" "$WORKTREE"; then
   809	        note_warning "warm-worktree.sh failed for $WORKTREE; falling back to a cold build"
   810	      fi
   811	    elif [ "${MIPSTARRE_CI_REQUIRE_WARMER:-}" = "1" ]; then
   812	      printf 'ERROR: %s is missing and MIPSTARRE_CI_REQUIRE_WARMER=1.\n' "$SCRIPT_DIR/warm-worktree.sh"
   813	      exit "$EXIT_TOOL_MISSING"
   814	    else
   815	      note_warning "local/bin/warm-worktree.sh not found; building $BRANCH from scratch (slow, but correct)"
   816	    fi
   817	  fi
   818	
   819	  require_tool lake "install elan (https://github.com/leanprover/elan) and re-run"
   820

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	#
     3	# usage: local/bin/ci.sh <pr-number> [options]
     4	#
     5	#   Local replacement for .github/workflows/pr-ci.yml.  Runs the same eight
     6	#   jobs (build, blueprint-render, paper-gaps, blueprint-sync, file-length,
     7	#   proof-debt, proof-evasion, statement-origin) against the worktree of the
     8	#   PR's branch, with the same per-area change gating, and records the result
     9	#   where GitHub is the source of truth: one `local-ci/<step>` commit status
    10	#   per step plus `local-ci/summary`, all bound to the exact tested head SHA,
    11	#   and one idempotent manifest comment on the PR.
    12	#
    13	#   <pr-number>        GitHub PR number (7 or 0007).  There is no prs/ tree
    14	#                      any more; the branch and base come from the PR itself
    15	#                      via local/bin/gh_common.py pr-view.
    16	#
    17	#   --worktree PATH    Use PATH as the branch worktree instead of resolving it
    18	#                      from `git worktree list` / .worktrees/<branch>.
    19	#   --base REF         Override the base branch reported by GitHub (default:
    20	#                      the PR's base ref, else main).
    21	#   --only STEP        Run only STEP (repeatable).  Gating still applies unless
    22	#                      --force-all is given.  Makes the run PARTIAL.
    23	#   --force-all        Ignore change gating; run every step.
    24	#   --skip-build       Record the build step as skipped (operator override for
    25	#                      a machine that must not compile right now).  Makes the
    26	#                      run PARTIAL.
    27	#   --dry-run          Resolve, gate and print the plan; run nothing, write
    28	#                      nothing, post nothing.
    29	#   -h, --help         This message.
    30	#
    31	# Outputs
    32	#   local-ci/<step> + local-ci/summary     commit statuses on the tested SHA
    33	#   PR comment <!-- mipstarre-ci-manifest pr=N -->   step table + manifest JSON
    34	#   ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-manifests/pr<N>-<sha>.json    per-step manifest
    35	#   ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-logs/<N>/<sha>/<step>.log     step logs (runtime)
    36	#   results/telemetry/builds.jsonl         one ci-build line when build ran
    37	#
    38	#   A PARTIAL run (--only / --skip-build / --dry-run) posts NOTHING to GitHub
    39	#   and writes <sha>.partial.json instead: a debugging run must not be able to
    40	#   hand the review or merge gate a verdict it did not earn.
    41	#
    42	# Exit status
    43	#   0  every gating step passed or was legitimately skipped
    44	#   1  at least one gating step failed or could not run, or the head moved
    45	#      under the run (the per-step statuses stand; no local-ci/summary)
    46	#   2  the run could not start (unknown PR, missing worktree, unresolvable
    47	#      base, local head != the PR's head) or its verdict could not be recorded
    48	#      on GitHub — fail closed, never a local fallback record
    49	#
    50	# Environment
    51	#   MIPSTARRE_GITHUB_REPO           owner/repo, as read by gh_common.py
    52	#   MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT            default ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev
    53	#   MIPSTARRE_FULL_BUILD_LOCK       default $CACHE_ROOT/.full-build-lock
    54	#                                   (must equal cache-warmer.sh/warm-worktree.sh:
    55	#                                   one path, one mutex)
    56	#   MIPSTARRE_CI_BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_S  default 14400 (4h) wait for the build lock
    57	#   MIPSTARRE_FULL_BUILD_LOCK_STALE_S default 10800 (3h) — applies ONLY to a
    58	#                                   lock whose owner stamp is unreadable; a
    59	#                                   lock with a live owner pid is never broken
    60	#   MIPSTARRE_CI_REQUIRE_WARMER=1   fail the build step if warm-worktree.sh is
    61	#                                   missing instead of doing a cold build
    62	#   MIPSTARRE_CI_ALLOW_COLD_FETCH=1 let the build step materialise .lake/packages
    63	#                                   itself instead of demanding worktree-setup.sh
    64	#
    65	# There is deliberately no LOCAL_CI_ENABLED kill switch: a disabled CI would
    66	# hand the merge gate a green light it never earned.  See local/protocols/ci.md.
    67	
    68	# shellcheck disable=SC2329  # step bodies and the trap handler run indirectly
    69	
    70	set -euo pipefail
    71	
    72	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    73	# Constants
    74	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    75	
    76	SCRIPT_PATH="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/$(basename "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")"
    77	SCRIPT_DIR="$(dirname "$SCRIPT_PATH")"
    78	
    79	STEP_NAMES="build blueprint-render paper-gaps blueprint-sync file-length proof-debt proof-evasion statement-origin"
    80	
    81	# Step exit codes with a meaning beyond "the command failed".
    82	EXIT_TOOL_MISSING=91
    83	
    84	CACHE_ROOT="${MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT:-$HOME/.cache/mipstarre-dev}"
    85	FULL_BUILD_LOCK="${MIPSTARRE_FULL_BUILD_LOCK:-$CACHE_ROOT/.full-build-lock}"
    86	BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_S="${MIPSTARRE_CI_BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_S:-14400}"
    87	BUILD_LOCK_STALE_S="${MIPSTARRE_FULL_BUILD_LOCK_STALE_S:-10800}"
    88	
    89	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    90	# Utilities
    91	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    92	
    93	info() { printf 'ci.sh: %s\n' "$*"; }
    94	warn() { printf 'ci.sh: warning: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
    95	
    96	die() {
    97	  printf 'ci.sh: error: %s\n' "$*" >&2
    98	  exit 2
    99	}
   100	
   101	iso_now() { date +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z; }
   102	epoch_now() { date +%s; }
   103	
   104	# Git hooks and Lake disagree about GIT_DIR: a lake invocation that inherits
   105	# the hook's git environment resolves nested package repositories against the
   106	# wrong repo.  Same subshell trick as .githooks/pre-push:19-24.
   107	run_outside_git_env() (
   108	  for _name in $(git rev-parse --local-env-vars); do
   109	    unset "$_name" || true
   110	  done
   111	  "$@"
   112	)
   113	
   114	# Locks are advisory mkdir-based lease directories, matching the hot-main
   115	# writer lease convention in local/protocols/build-cache.md.
   116	HELD_LOCKS=""
   117	
   118	lock_age_s() {
   119	  # $1 = lock dir.  Prints the age in seconds of its owner stamp, or a huge
   120	  # number when the stamp is unreadable (treat as stale).
   121	  local _stamp="$1/owner"
   122	  if [ ! -f "$_stamp" ]; then
   123	    printf '%s\n' 999999999
   124	    return 0
   125	  fi
   126	  local _mtime
   127	  _mtime="$(stat -f %m "$_stamp" 2>/dev/null || stat -c %Y "$_stamp" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
   128	  printf '%s\n' "$(( $(epoch_now) - _mtime ))"
   129	}
   130	
   131	lock_owner_alive() {
   132	  local _stamp="$1/owner"
   133	  [ -f "$_stamp" ] || return 1
   134	  local _pid
   135	  _pid="$(head -n 1 "$_stamp" 2>/dev/null || true)"
   136	  case "$_pid" in
   137	    ''|*[!0-9]*) return 1 ;;
   138	  esac
   139	  kill -0 "$_pid" 2>/dev/null
   140	}
   141	
   142	# acquire_lock <dir> <wait_seconds> <stale_seconds> <tag>
   143	# Returns 0 on success, 1 on timeout.  A lock whose owner process is ALIVE is
   144	# NEVER broken, regardless of age: the parent workflow exempts main-branch
   145	# (cache-seeding) runs from cancellation, and the local analog is that a
   146	# running full build is always allowed to finish (the initial cold build took
   147	# ~7 h; see results/telemetry/builds.jsonl).  The stale threshold applies only
   148	# when the owner stamp is unreadable, so an interrupted mkdir cannot wedge the
   149	# machine forever.
   150	acquire_lock() {
   151	  local _dir="$1" _wait="$2" _stale="$3" _tag="$4"
   152	  local _waited=0
   153	  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$_dir")"
   154	  while ! mkdir "$_dir" 2>/dev/null; do
   155	    if lock_owner_alive "$_dir"; then
   156	      : # live owner: wait below, never break
   157	    elif [ -f "$_dir/owner" ] || [ -f "$_dir/info" ]; then
   158	      warn "breaking stale lock $_dir (owner process is dead)"
   159	      rm -rf "$_dir"
   160	      continue
   161	    elif [ "$(lock_age_s "$_dir")" -gt "$_stale" ]; then
   162	      warn "breaking stale lock $_dir (no owner stamp, older than ${_stale}s)"
   163	      rm -rf "$_dir"
   164	      continue
   165	    fi
   166	    if [ "$_waited" -ge "$_wait" ]; then
   167	      return 1
   168	    fi
   169	    if [ "$_waited" -eq 0 ]; then
   170	      info "waiting for lock $_dir (held by pid $(head -n 1 "$_dir/owner" 2>/dev/null || echo '?'))"
   171	    fi
   172	    sleep 5
   173	    _waited=$(( _waited + 5 ))
   174	  done
